newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed with a technical correction on the domestic A share markets offset by one new issue, traders said.

The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract fell slightly to 9.08 percent from 9.30 percent on Wednesday. Total turnover of the six-contract market surged to 11 million lots from 3.6 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"The A share markets had a correction after consecutive gains over the past few days, which resulted in some institutions withdrawing from the repo market," a trader said.

But the new issue of Huangshan Tourism Development Co Ltd on the Shanghai stock exchange today and a new issue on the Shenzhen stock exchange on Friday supported the contracts, and made trading more active than Wednesday, traders said.
"The seven-day contract moved at a high level for most of the session today due to the new issues, but was depressed by institutional selling in late trading," said another trader.
Traders said they expected the rates to move in a narrow range on Friday with the three-day contract falling.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Thursday because of the low coupon rate on the latest batch of state debt.

The Finance Minitry announced on Wednesday that it would issue 40 billion yuan worth in three-year treasury notes in May at an annual coupon of 9.18 percent, the third batch of state debt to be issued this year.
"The coupon is much lower than the yields of existing contracts, which pushed up prices," a trader said.
The most actively traded three-year bond that matures in August 1999 rose to 107.2 yuan from 106.9 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market rose sharply to 1.6 million lots from 995,119 lots.
Traders said they believed the spots would move up slightly in the next few trading days.
